cacheTTL.description: How long a source's discovered skills and head commit are reused. A failed read is retried after 30 seconds and keeps the last good listing.

fullnameOverride.description: Override the fully qualified release name.

apiUrl.description: GitHub API base URL: discovery, pinning, the person's access to a private repository, and `GET /user` for a forwarded GitHub token.

secretName.description: Existing Secret in the release namespace of skill-manager's read-only GitHub App, with the keys `app-id`, `installation-id` and `private-key` (PEM): skills are discovered and pinned with the App's installation tokens, at the App's rate limit. Mutually exclusive with `tokenSecret`. Empty (and no `tokenSecret`): anonymous, public repositories only.

enabled.description: Private skill repositories, checked as the person: GitHub decides whether they can read one. With `tokenExchange`, the MCP tools and the REST API fetch the person's user token of skill-manager's GitHub App (`app`) for a private repository only and ask GitHub as them. Off: `tokenExchange` is refused.

audience.description: RFC 8693 audience that releases the grant, also the App named in the `grant_required` answer and in the MCPServer's `auth.providerApps`. Required with `tokenEndpoint`.

caSecretName.description: Optional existing Secret with `ca.crt` for the broker's private CA.

clientID.description: Confidential client ID at the broker. Empty: read from the Secret's `client-id` key.

clientSecret.description: Client secret, rendered into the Secret `<fullname>-github-token-exchange`; prefer `existingSecret`.

existingSecret.description: Existing Secret in the release namespace with `client-secret` (and `client-id` when `clientID` is empty).

tokenEndpoint.description: RFC 8693 token endpoint (muster's broker) that releases the person's user token of skill-manager's GitHub App when a private repository needs it; `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` as the person then decides. Listings never ask for it: without the grant they leave out the private sources and name `audience` under `grantRequired`; pinning or reading a private skill answers `grant_required`. Needs `github.enabled` and `oauth.enabled`. Empty: off.

key.description: Key of the token in that Secret.

name.description: Deprecated: prefer `app`. Existing Secret in the release namespace with a static GitHub token skills are read with.

global.description: Global values shared between all subcharts and the platform.

tag.description: Image tag. Defaults to the chart appVersion.

auth.description: How muster authenticates to this server; rendered only with `oauth.enabled`. `forwardToken` makes muster forward the session's Dex id_token byte-identical (the SSO path this chart trusts through its trusted audiences); with `github.tokenExchange` the CR also lists its `audience` under `auth.providerApps`. `requiredAudiences` are extra audiences that token must carry — the Dex cross-client audience the kube-apiserver trusts (`dex-k8s-authenticator` on Giant Swarm clusters; agentlab's is `kubernetes`); muster requests them at login, so users re-login after a change. They are trusted as bearer audiences by construction, since the server's trusted audiences are `oauth.trustedAudiences` plus this list.

github.description: Deprecated and ignored: the GitHub App pin is replaced by `github.tokenExchange`, which fetches the person's grant only for a private repository.

autoStart.description: Start the server connection when muster initializes.

displayName.description: Name the Dev Portal shows for this server, rendered as the MCPServer's `ui.giantswarm.io/display-name` annotation. Empty renders no annotation.

enabled.description: Register this server with muster by rendering an `mcpservers.muster.giantswarm.io` CR in the release namespace. Tools then appear as `x_<name>_<tool>`.

labels.description: Extra labels on the MCPServer CR.

name.description: MCPServer CR name (drives the tool prefix).

timeout.description: How long muster waits for a tool's answer, in seconds (the MCPServer's `spec.timeout`, 1 to 300): muster's default.

allowInternet.description: Allow egress on 443 to every destination: GitHub, OCI registries and an external Dex. Vanilla NetworkPolicy cannot select by name; narrow with egressCIDRs instead when the addresses are known. With `oauth.enabled`, Dex's own port is opened from its issuer URL as well: its namespace for an in-cluster `<svc>.<namespace>.svc` host (e.g. port 5556), every address otherwise.

enabled.description: Create a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy for the pod.

ingressNamespaces.description: Namespaces allowed to reach the MCP endpoint and the REST API (label kubernetes.io/metadata.name), besides the release namespace. List muster's, agent-manager's and the portal's namespaces when they run elsewhere, or they cannot reach the server.

metricsNamespaces.description: Namespaces allowed to scrape the metrics port (label kubernetes.io/metadata.name), when `observability.metrics.enabled`.

allowPublicClientRegistration.description: Accept unauthenticated dynamic client registration (labs only).

baseURL.description: Public base URL of this server: the issuer of its own OAuth metadata (https, or http on loopback). Empty derives `https://<fullname>.<global.domain>` when `global.domain` is set.

allowPrivateURLs.description: Let the issuer resolve to a private or loopback address (an in-cluster Dex).

caSecret.description: Secret with the CA of a Dex that serves a private certificate; mounted and passed as the `dex-ca-file` flag. Empty name falls back to `global.identity.ca.secretName` / `global.identity.ca.key`.

clientID.description: Dex OAuth client ID. Empty falls back to `global.identity.clientId`.

issuerURL.description: Dex issuer URL. Empty falls back to `global.identity.issuerUrl`.

enabled.description: Make skill-manager an OAuth 2.1 resource server (mcp-oauth): the MCP endpoint and the REST API require a bearer token Dex issued, validated against Dex's JWKS when its audience is in `trustedAudiences`. muster forwards the session's Dex id_token (`muster.mcpServer.auth`); agent-manager and the portal forward the person's. Deprecated: a REST call may instead carry the person's GitHub token as the bearer and the id_token in `X-Muster-Id-Token`, as agent-manager forwards them on its GitHub registration: the GitHub login then opens the private repositories the person can read. Off: no authentication at all, and private repositories are refused; only for a server nothing but a trusted proxy can reach. Off by default only because it needs the installation's Dex: the `agent-platform` meta chart turns it on.

existingSecret.description: Existing Secret with the Dex client secret under `dex-client-secret`. Empty falls back to `global.identity.existingSecret`; without that, the chart renders a Secret from `oauth.dex.clientSecret`.

allowPrivateIPs.description: Let Dex's JWKS endpoint resolve to a private address when validating forwarded tokens (an in-cluster Dex).

trustedAudiences.description: OAuth client IDs whose Dex id_tokens are accepted as bearer tokens (SSO token forwarding). Empty falls back to `[global.identity.clientId]`, the platform client MCP clients and the muster CLI log in with. The server trusts the union of this list and `muster.mcpServer.auth.requiredAudiences` (in that order, without duplicates): every token muster forwards carries the required audiences by construction and they are what the kube-apiserver trusts, so a portal session — whose id_token carries them but not the platform client — is accepted without listing its client here.

enabled.description: Serve Prometheus metrics on `GET /metrics` of the `metrics` port: `mcp_server_operation_duration_seconds` per tool and `http_server_request_duration_seconds` for the MCP endpoint. Off, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none`: nothing is served.

port.description: Port of the metrics listener, apart from the MCP port so the OAuth guard never covers it.

endpoint.description: OTLP collector URL for traces, e.g. `http://otlp-gateway.kube-system.svc:4317` (gRPC) or `https://tempo.example.com:4318` (with protocol `http/protobuf`). Empty exports nothing; inbound `traceparent` headers still propagate. With `networkPolicy.enabled` the policy opens egress to it: the Service's namespace for an in-cluster host, every address otherwise.

headers.description: OTLP headers (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`), e.g. `X-Scope-OrgID=giantswarm` for a multi-tenant collector.

resourceAttributes.description: Resource attributes appended to the downward-API `k8s.pod.name`, `k8s.namespace.name` and `k8s.node.name`.

sampler.description: `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`. The parent-based default follows the caller's sampling decision and samples `samplerArg` of the traces that start here.

registries.description: The registries (host or host:port) an OCI skill or plugin may come from. No other registry, and none by IP address, is asked; a token realm must be on the registry or another listed host. Empty: no OCI skills.

replicaCount.description: Number of replicas. The server keeps no MCP session state and every replica validates forwarded Dex tokens, so two or more are fine for muster, agent-manager and the portal; each keeps its own discovery cache. Tokens the server issues itself (a client signing in to it directly) live in one replica's memory and fail on another.

revisionHistoryLimit.description: Number of old ReplicaSets retained for rollback.

enabled.description: Render a ServiceMonitor for the `metrics` port. Also needs `observability.metrics.enabled`.

interval.description: Scrape interval; empty uses the Prometheus Operator default.

labels.description: Labels on the ServiceMonitor, beside the chart's own. The Giant Swarm observability platform routes a scrape to a Mimir tenant by `observability.giantswarm.io/tenant`; a monitor without it writes to no tenant.

key.description: Key of the token in that Secret.

secretName.description: Existing Secret in the release namespace with a bearer the REST API admits as the platform's own caller, no person, for agent-manager's `migrate`; no readability check applies to it. Needs `oauth.enabled`. Empty: none.

sources.description: The skill sources: each a github.com repository URL or `{url, ref, path, readOnly}`. `ref` is a branch, tag or commit (empty: the default branch): what discovery reads and what a skill of the source without its own ref pins. `path` is the directory scanned (empty: the whole repository). `readOnly` is reported, not enforced. A repository given twice needs paths that do not contain each other.
